episode_title: #19 - Jack Lundin basar över Stockholmsbörsens tyngsta gruvbolag Lundin Mining

stock_segments.discussion_summary: Comprehensive discussion about Lundin Mining, the third-generation family mining business now producing over 400,000 tons of copper annually across six operations worldwide. Jack explains their disciplined growth strategy, focus on copper, and position as a cost-competitive copper producer. The conversation covers their major assets in Chile and the emerging Vicuña district, sustainability initiatives, and long-term vision for the company.

quotes.speaker: Jack Lundin
quotes.text: Lundin Mining is our flagship base metals business in the Lundin Group. We've got six operations worldwide and one mega growth project in Argentina. So we have two mines in Europe, one in the United States, and three operating mines and one mega project in South America. We're primarily focused on copper. About 75% of our revenues are geared towards copper, but we also produce a substantial amount of zinc.

quotes.speaker: Jack Lundin
quotes.text: Lundin Mining did about 315,000 tonnes of copper last year in 2023. And with the acquisition we made last year, we're looking at doing closer to 400,000 tons of copper this year in the upper end of our guidance ranges. So we're definitely scaling up.

quotes.speaker: Jack Lundin
quotes.text: When we've seen over the last few weeks here, copper going up from around $3.85 to $5 a pound, we've seen the share price appreciation following that trend at Lundin Mining. So we are heavily geared towards to the copper price.

quotes.speaker: Jack Lundin
quotes.text: We're looking at putting ourselves in a position to get ourselves into development as soon as possible. This year is very important for Jose Maria because we're looking at forming fiscal stability with the government of Argentina and really the province of San Juan where Jose Maria is located.

quotes.speaker: Jack Lundin
quotes.text: I want the company to be seen as the go-to name for copper companies in our sector. And what I mean by that is a company that continues to drive value, a company that has a fantastic reputation, that is seen as a responsible and reputable firm in all of the jurisdictions that we're operating in.

quotes.speaker: Jack Lundin
quotes.text: For Lundin Mining, we've set a target of reducing our overall greenhouse gas emissions by 35% by the year 2030. In Chile, most of our assets are almost 100% of the power that's being generated for Candelaria and Caserones is done with renewable energy.

custom: Candelaria and Caserones 34% and 35% of revenue respectively

bull_case: Expanding production from 315k to 400k tons copper
Strategic acquisitions in Vicuña district creating synergies
Geared to copper price which is in tight supply
bear_case: Copper price volatility and cyclical nature
Capital intensive nature of new mine development
Long lead times for new projects (17 years average)
catalysts: AI and green transition driving demand
Eagle mine free cash flow generation
risks: Environmental and social license to operate

insights.quote: Oftentimes, you're putting the same amount of energy to build something small as you are, to build something big. So it goes back to what I've been saying on this podcast, which is make sure that it's driving value. And if you can drive value at scale, that is the biggest opportunity that we look to seek out.
insights.summary: When building ventures, invest the same energy in big opportunities as small ones, as scale maximizes impact
insights.speaker: Jack Lundin

insights.quote: On average, it takes around 17 years from exploration success. So when you make a discovery to when you can actually bring that production online, it can take, on average, 10 years to just get a mine permitted to be built.
insights.summary: New copper mines take 17 years from discovery to production due to permitting, development, and financing challenges
insights.speaker: Jack Lundin

insights.quote: When you look at the biggest mineral or oil and gas deposits worldwide. Usually they continue to grow, and there's a lot of resource extension capabilities or exploration upside potential. So Zinc Reuven has provided some of the most significant returns in the history of the company because of our continuous replacement of resources.
insights.summary: Large resource deposits tend to grow over time through resource extension, generating outsized returns through continuous exploration
insights.speaker: Jack Lundin

insights.quote: You need to be planning for these operations to run continuously. Of course, we have scheduled maintenance downtime when we're doing, you know, repairs and whatnot a couple of times a year for each of our operations. But to be that reactionary and try and shut down a mine if the price isn't where we would like it to be, it's impossible to run the business that way.
insights.summary: Mining operations cannot be easily turned on/off based on price fluctuations; must plan for continuous operations through cycles
insights.speaker: Jack Lundin

insights.quote: So what we can control is safety, culture and costs. And if we can do those well, then we'll be able to, you know, weather the storms in the cyclical nature of our business.
insights.summary: Focus on controlling what you can - safety, culture, and costs - to navigate cyclical commodity markets
insights.speaker: Jack Lundin

insights.quote: Each time we focus too hard on share price in the immediate term, you maybe might not be making the best decisions for the long term. So, you know, I think share price appreciation is a byproduct of delivering on what our targets are and continuing to drive value.
insights.summary: Share price is a byproduct of execution and value creation, not something to optimize directly
insights.speaker: Jack Lundin

summary: Interview with Jack Lundin, CEO of Lundin Mining, discussing the copper market tightness, supply constraints requiring 17 years for new mines, and strong demand drivers from AI and green transition. Lundin Mining produces 400,000 tons copper annually with disciplined growth strategy, expanding in South America's Vicuña district.
key_takeaways: Copper supply is tightening with ~900k tons coming offline in 2024 alone
New copper mines take 17 years from discovery to production
Lundin Mining scaled copper production from 315k to 400k tons
Vicuña district acquisitions (Jose Maria, Caserones) create strategic synergies
AI and green transition driving unprecedented copper demand
Company focuses on safety, culture, and costs to navigate cycles
